cues.text: Taking notes is easy.
Knowing what to revise,
and when, across many subjects, is the hard part.
Haunted Notes turns your notes into ghosts
and remembers the revision schedule for you.
You only have to remember the answers.
Add notes four ways.
Type them, speak with your microphone,
snap a photo of printed text, or upload an audio recording.
Audio files and photos are processed on your own device,
and the live microphone uses your browser's speech service.
Each note is split into fill-in-the-blank flashcards,
so even a long lecture becomes a short set of questions.
Every note becomes a haunted room.
Each flashcard you have not mastered is a ghost,
and the weaker your memory of it, the more menacing it looks.
The meter at the top shows how crowded your haunting is.
Start a quiz and fill in each blank.
Stuck? Ask for a hint, or reveal the answer.
A wrong answer breaks your quiz streak and sends the ghost
back to the start of its review ladder.
A right answer banishes it. Small typos on long words are forgiven,
and the answer is never hidden in the page before you respond.
When the round ends, review only the cards you missed.
Banished ghosts do not stay gone.
A fixed ladder brings each one back after
two, three, five, then seven days,
so you never track dates yourself.
Skip ahead, and the ghosts that are due return, glowing orange.
Your study insights show your day streak,
what you reviewed today, your accuracy this week,
and your weakest rooms.
Your notes live in your browser.
Export a backup any time, and import it back
with a safety check before anything is merged.
Haunted Notes was built with Kiro, using specs, steering files, hooks,
a custom UI reviewer agent, a Playwright MCP server,
and property-based tests that caught real bugs.
You remember the answers.
Haunted Notes remembers when.
The link and source code are below.
Kiroween 2026, Frankenstein.

cuesMeasuredWith: startMs = end of the quiet gap before the phrase in the WAV (50 ms windows, rms < 350); the first cue of a clip is 0. Chapters 1, 5 and 9: the words in each stretch of speech were also recognised per stretch with the offline Windows recogniser, to place the splits inside sentences. estimated = split inside a phrase with no gap, placed by word count.
